domain: Dispute-bearing data modeling — where a declared, machine-checkable ontology (inverse, symmetry, domain/range, schema version) and a commentary apparatus (citable address, attributed layer, preserved machloket, first-class teiku) are required of the same field
tension: Parent A treats contradiction as a defect the declared axioms exist to make impossible: a validator's job is to refuse a disputed edge until one value survives. Parent B treats contradiction as content the corpus exists to preserve: resolving a machloket without retaining both claims, both sources and the deciding authority destroys information the resolved state cannot recover. Satisfy A by writing one winner per pair and B's record is gone; satisfy B by committing both claims and A's inverse/symmetry invariant is violated by design. This lens does not choose. It investigates every place in the plan where the same byte is asked to be both a checkable invariant and a durable record of a ruling, and reports what breaks there.
fused_primitive: The dispute-bearing assertion: a relation or type assignment that is at once axiomatically typed (inverse, symmetry, domain/range, schema version) and citably addressed, layer-marked, attributed, and markable as permanently unresolved.
axioms: A contradiction that has been ruled is a different object from a contradiction that was never asserted; a schema that cannot tell them apart has not reconciled anything, it has deleted.

An invariant can only be enforced against an assertion it can name, and an authority can only be attached to an assertion that can be cited — the identity-less edge fails both at once, and it is the same missing field.

'Stands undecided' must be a declared member of the type system rather than the absence of a value; a gate demanding one value per edge before that member exists manufactures a consensus no axiom derived and no authority signed.

Classification is two records, not one: the label a validator checks and the derivation a reader audits. A scheme carrying only the label can neither express 'no good fit' nor prove it still discriminates.
An authority precedence rule is real only when it is versioned and cited per edge; a tie-break stated in prose resolves nothing that either a validator or a later reader can act on.

Derived structure must be reproducible from a stated definition over a frozen, citable edition; a count quoted from an unnamed snapshot is neither checkable nor returnable-to, and it will be quoted again after the data under it changes.
A schema version must carry forward which assignments were forced, so growth in the type system reopens exactly the rulings it invalidates and no others.

Merging sources into one file is a provenance operation before it is a correctness one: unless each generation's additions stay layer-marked, no invariant can constrain a machine gloss differently from a received claim.
primitives: the ruled edge — a relation carrying its winning claim, its losing claim, its deciding authority and its rationale, all machine-readable
the sanctioned contradiction — an axiom-level exemption that distinguishes a preserved dispute from an invariant violation
the teiku type — 'unresolved' as a declared member of the relation/type enum: legal to commit, legal to gate, legal to render
the edge address — a stable id an invariant can name and a decision record can cite
the derivation-bearing classification — issue_type plus the stated resemblance argument plus an explicit 'no good fit' member
the versioned precedence rule — engine-vs-catalog authority stated per edge, with the schema version it was ruled under
the layer marker — which generation and which producer (human author, scraper, Jev, regeneration pass) wrote this field
the citable edition — a frozen graph state over which derived structure such as the 94 reinforcing loops is defined and reproducible
the forced-assignment ledger — the record of which rulings a schema-version bump must reopen
failure_mode: Single-parent defects: by construction it drops any finding either parent could reach alone, so it under-reports real and severe but structurally simple problems. It supplements fd-ontology-knowledgegraph and fd-talmudic-apparatus; it never replaces them.
Visual and perceptual legibility — layout seeding, labels, legend, edge styling, density, mobile, accessibility — belongs wholly to fd-netviz-legibility and is invisible here.
Machine-side cost: payload size, build time, render cost and the runtime price of validating or deriving at scale.
Prose quality and whether a description reads as a definition or a crisis headline — it judges what a field records, not how it reads.
Statistical validity of the Jev pass — sampling, lift over a baseline, dual-rater agreement, grounding-guard design — except where it leaves a schema or provenance residue.
Proportionality and staffing: it will propose provenance structure without checking that one maintainer can author and carry it, so its recommendations need a cost check it cannot perform.
The first-time visitor's comprehension, which is the brainstorm's actual purpose: this lens judges the record, not the reader's experience of it.
intersection_rule: A finding is in scope only if both parents are load-bearing. Every finding must carry an intersection_justification naming what the ontology parent contributes, what the apparatus parent contributes, and why either alone would miss or misdiagnose it.
